title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives election in California's 1st Congressional District
description: This race for California's 1st Congressional District takes place under newly redrawn boundaries approved by voters via Proposition 50, shifting the district southward to include parts of Sonoma County and making it more competitive (Cook Partisan Voting Index D+7). The seat became vacant after the death of longtime Republican incumbent Doug LaMalfa in January 2026; a special election held concurrently with the June 2 primary was won by Republican James Gallagher, who now serves the remainder of LaMalfa's term. The November general election will determine who represents the district for the next two-year term starting in January 2027, with Republican incumbent Gallagher facing Democratic state Senator Mike McGuire in a race that could factor into the national fight for control of the U.S. House.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the 2026 general election in California's 1st Congressional District as of the research date.

candidates.name: James Gallagher
candidates.summary: James Gallagher is a Republican U.S. Representative who was sworn into office on June 10, 2026, after winning the special election to succeed the late Doug LaMalfa. He previously served in the California State Assembly from 2014 to 2026, including three years as Assembly Minority Leader, and served on the Sutter County Board of Supervisors. Gallagher is a lawyer and partner in his family's fifth-generation rice and walnut farming operation.

candidates.name: Mike McGuire
candidates.summary: Mike McGuire is a Democratic California State Senator who has represented the 2nd Senate District since 2014, serving as Senate Majority Leader (2022-2024) and President pro tempore (2024-2025). He previously served on the Sonoma County Board of Supervisors and the Healdsburg City Council, and was first elected to public office at age 19 on the Healdsburg School Board. McGuire is a fourth-generation North Coast farmer and holds a BA in political science from Sonoma State University.
